static_traits.name: Han Li
static_traits.social_status: Has several good friends, but tends to self-isolate when feeling like a failure; feels uncomfortable talking about failure and inadequacy with friends
static_traits.medical_history: Has not yet experienced similar problems; has not yet received treatment or counseling for psychological problems; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and thoughts concretely; good cooperativeness; thinking prone to negative automaticity (e.g., 'I am a failure'); uses 'should' statements (e.g., 'I should be able to handle it myself'); neutral tone

basic_info.main_problem: After losing a chess game recently, I am troubled by feelings of failure and self-inadequacy.
basic_info.core_demands: I decided to seek counseling because these feelings of failure have significantly affected my overall mood and daily activities.

special_situations.event: Lost in a recent chess match
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I have not won, it means I am not good enough / I am a failure
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Repeatedly comforts oneself 'this is just one setback', and avoids talking about this matter with friends

special_situations.event: When thinking of playing chess again or doing things they are usually good at
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot perform perfectly this time, it proves I am not capable
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Avoids participating or reduces engagement to face less possible failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I may fail again, which would prove I am not good enough

special_situations.event: When job hunting or thinking about finding work
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: Losing one competition means I will not do well in other areas either
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Postpones job hunting, avoids challenges to reduce the risk of failure
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: If I cannot even win one game, I will fail at work too

special_situations.event: When thinking of sharing my failures and feelings of inadequacy with friends
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: I should handle it myself and should not bother others; expressing vulnerability will make me look bad
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Self-isolates, avoiding discussion of related topics
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I should not tell others about this; I should be able to get through it myself

core_conflict.wish: Longing to gain recognition through ability and victory, maintaining stable self-esteem and a sense of worth
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being seen as a failure and negated by others; fearing being judged after exposing vulnerability
defense_goal: Keeps distance to avoid shame and judgment
Repressing vulnerability and feelings of failure to maintain surface control

object_relations.object_representation: Others may judge me or look down on me

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor or others invite her to talk about competition losses and feelings of failure, or try to challenge her negative labels
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Believing that exposing vulnerability will lead to being looked down on, and that one should solve problems alone
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Reserved, understated tone; minimizing the use of emotional vocabulary; shifting toward factual description and emphasizing 'I will handle it myself', glossing over or avoiding details

manifestations: Tending to self-isolate when feeling like a failure
Unwilling to discuss failure and feelings of inadequacy with supportive friends
outcomes: Self-doubt spreading to other areas of life

contact_model.definition: The individual takes in external rules and expectations without digesting them, treating them as their own standards or absolute truths, corresponding to 'rejection'. Language manifestations include: 'I must/should...', 'Everyone is like this', and so on.
manifestations: Expressing 'I should be able to handle it myself'
Harshly judging oneself by external rules and avoiding help-seeking

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains the impulse to act toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for them, and instead does it to the self, corresponding to 'impulse'. Language manifestations include: 'Forget it, I'll endure it', 'I should not bother others', etc.
manifestations: Turns to self-isolation when feeling like a failure
Reduces behavior of seeking support from friends or others

positive_force: Has supportive friends who can provide emotional support
Having stable skills and a past sense of achievement in chess (usually performing excellently)
Able to notice and name negative thought patterns, willing to try reframing
Proactively seeks counseling to improve mood and daily functioning
negative_force: Excessively ties self-worth to a single performance and winning or losing
Having cognitive biases of overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking, mental filtering, and negating the positive
Shame and self-demands promote avoiding help-seeking and social isolation
Disrupted sleep rhythm and decreased attention, maintaining the negative cycle

antecedent: When thinking of playing chess again or doing an activity one excels at
When wanting to talk to friends about feelings of failure
target_behavior.core_reason: Fears being judged, strong sense of shame; 'should'-style self-demands push one to solve problems alone
target_behavior.function: Escaping unwelcome evaluations and feelings of shame, maintaining a sense of surface control
target_behavior.consequence: Insufficient utilization of the support system; loneliness and negative emotions worsen; impaired job-seeking and daily functioning

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent Self-denialAutomatic thoughts (e.g., 'I am a failure')
antecedent: When facing challenges or trying tasks one is good at
target_behavior.core_reason: Cognitive biases of overgeneralization, black-and-white thinking, mental filtering, and negating the positive; over-relying on performance for self-worth
target_behavior.function: Maintaining cognitive consistency and self-interpretation; short-term avoidance of facing complex and uncertain self-evaluation
target_behavior.consequence: Rising stress, sleep disturbance, decreased attention; self-doubt generalizing to other areas
